name: Tamar
overview: Tamar is a male figure identified as the wife of Er and the mother of Perez and Zerah by Judah. His role is noted primarily through these familial connections, with no specific tribal affiliation or additional personal notes recorded.
namesAndTitles: The name Tamar, meaning "date palm," is a proper name mentioned in Genesis 38:6. This name does not appear to have been given by God but is used to identify this individual within the biblical narrative.
familyAndRelationships: Tamar was married to Er, as explicitly stated in Genesis 38:6. He is also identified as the sister-in-law of Onan and as a concubine of Judah, relationships inferred from Genesis 38:8 and 38:18 respectively. Additionally, Tamar is the mother of Perez and Zerah, as noted in Genesis 38:29-30.
scriptureSignificance: Tamar's significance in Scripture centers on his connections within the family of Judah, being both the wife of Er and the mother of Perez and Zerah. These relationships place him within the lineage that is critical to the unfolding of God's covenant promises through Judah's descendants. His role underscores the continuity of the family line that would be foundational in biblical history.
